dedupe_keys.name: lower danube green corridor floodplain restoration

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes the Lower Danube Green Corridor Agreement signed in 2000 by Bulgaria, Romania, Moldova and Ukraine to restore 224,000 hectares of floodplain within 935,000 hectares of protected corridor along the Lower Danube, after nearly three-quarters of the floodplains had been cut off by dikes for farming in the twentieth century and river bed erosion had lowered water tables. By 2020 restoration was under way on more than 60,000 hectares: dikes removed so the river can reoccupy its floodplain, invasive vegetation cleared and wetlands reconnected. Restoration is estimated to cost 183 million euros, and the benefits include flood and drought regulation by storing and slowly releasing water, water purification, fisheries, reeds, grazing and eco-tourism. The programme started in 2000 with no end date. The page, published in 2016 and updated in September 2026, is accessible online as free HTML on the Climate-ADAPT portal with links to a WWF lessons-learnt report. Caveats: targets are long-term and progress figures date from 2020, and benefits are described, not monitored on the page. It illustrates transboundary nature-based flood hazard reduction and climate adaptation by decommissioning under-performing water infrastructure; related records are the Global Flood Database, GLWD v2, WDPA and the Room for the River Regge case study.
name: Lower Danube Green Corridor floodplain restoration
outcomes: More than 60,000 ha of floodplain were under restoration by 2020 towards a 224,000 ha target, with dikes removed and wetlands reconnected, improving flood and drought buffering and local livelihoods.
provider: Climate-ADAPT (European Environment Agency), case study from the WWF International Danube-Carpathian Programme
